# `silk/platform/windows/process_image`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Interactive Windows process execution: inherit the terminal, environment,
and working directory, wait for the image, and return its exact exit status to the shell.

Import as `WindowsProcessImage` with `import silk.platform.windows.process_image as WindowsProcessImage`.

Public declarations: 6.

<a id="setVariableBytes"></a>

## `setVariableBytes`

```silk
pub effect fn setVariableBytes(name: &[u8], value: &[u8]) -> bool ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Sets a live Windows environment variable from canonical WTF-8 host bytes, replacing its value.
Returns false for an empty name, `=` in the name, NUL, invalid WTF-8, or an OS refusal.
Allocation failure remains an Effect. Previously captured `HostInput` snapshots do not change.

<a id="setVariableDefaultBytes"></a>

## `setVariableDefaultBytes`

```silk
pub effect fn setVariableDefaultBytes(name: &[u8], value: &[u8]) -> bool ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Sets a default from canonical WTF-8 host bytes, preserving an existing value, including empty.
Returns false for invalid WTF-8, NUL, an empty name, `=` in the name, or an OS refusal.
The presence check and update are separate calls; concurrent environment writers may race.

<a id="replace"></a>

## `replace`

```silk
pub effect fn replace(program: &Path, arguments: &[Bytes], directory: Option<&Path>) -> bool ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Runs an explicit executable with inherited standard streams and environment, in `directory`
when one is given and otherwise in this process's working directory. Returns false if setup
fails. On successful launch it waits and exits with the child's DWORD.

<a id="execute"></a>

## `execute`

```silk
pub effect fn execute(program: &Path, arguments: &[Bytes], directory: Option<&Path>) -> Option<u32> ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Runs an explicit executable with inherited standard streams and environment, in `directory`
when one is given and otherwise in this process's working directory, waits for it, and returns
its DWORD exit status.

### Details
The executable gets duplicates of this process's standard handles and no others. While it
runs, this process ignores Ctrl+C, so the child handles it.

### Gotchas
Returns none when setup fails, or the executable is a batch script (`.bat` or `.cmd`), which
would need a shell.
